title: fix: cap pull request CI jobs at fifteen minutes
author: karanray06
pr_body_excerpt:
- Adds a 15-minute limit to the four pull request CI jobs, preventing hung work from consuming the six-hour default.
- Leaves deployments, Docker builds, and other automation unchanged.
- Validated with actionlint and git diff --check.
- Addresses #14862. The Vitest/Cloudflare test-timeout investigation remains open.

gist.headline: No More Six-Hour Hangs
gist.blurb: The PR checks now know when to stop waiting for a stuck job. Four CI workers get a tidy 15-minute sand timer, while the rest of the automation garden keeps growing as before.
gist.summary: Added a 15-minute timeout to all four pull-request CI jobs in ci-pull-request-checks.yml, preventing hung checks from using GitHub Actions' six-hour default while leaving deployments and Docker builds unchanged.
gist.impact: Contributors get faster feedback when a pull-request check stalls, and CI capacity is preserved for work that is actually moving.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy garden-workshop scene where Polli, wearing a tiny mechanic tool belt, watches four small CRT terminal robots work beside matching 15-minute pixel sand timers; one sleepy stalled terminal is gently capped, while healthy code-plants continue growing in the background.
